driver: A unit's expected next-period level is read from a few periods of its own record, and for small units the record's spread is mostly chance, larger than the true differences between units; taking each unit's record at face value ranks the lucky small units low and the unlucky ones high, while the expected level weighs the unit's record against the pool by how much of its spread is signal.
driver_concrete: A twelve-person shop whose 2024 included one member's $140,000 claim has a three-year average far over the trust's, but its expected 2027 claims are only a little over the trust's level; a sixty-member employer with three quiet years is expected to cost nearly the trust's level too; the easy route raises the first and spares the second.
stump: The default path trends each employer's own 2023 to 2025 retained claims to 2027 and files CR104, CR109, CR136, CR167 and CR176 surcharged, because it never asks how much of a small employer's three years is chance: one member's large claim moves a forty-member employer's year by more than the employers truly differ, so the small employers with high experience are expected near the trust's level and under their claims components, and the small employers with low experience, whose claims components sit well under the trust's level, are expected over them.

differentiation.task130: task130's later architecture forecasts a group chosen for an extreme value in one period by carrying its value forward; here no group is chosen by its value and no period is extreme by selection: every employer's expected level is weighed against the pool by the signal share of its own three-year spread, which depends on its size.
differentiation.task479v3: architecture 3 trended a group's large claimants under a fixed specific deductible; here the deductible only caps the experience and the step is weighting each employer's experience by its credibility.
differentiation.task148: task148 models a queue drained by units that give up, the patience seen fully only for leavers; here nothing waits or leaves: each employer's expected claims are its noisy experience weighed against the pool's.
differentiation.task241: task241 reads a sensor's error against a reference displaced by movement of the medium; here no reference is displaced: the pool's own experience is the complement each small employer's chance-heavy record is weighed against.

lineage.driver: A record of past events on units is carried to the units as they now stand, and some units were raised after their events, so a past event counts again on a raised unit only where the event's recorded level stood above the unit's new threshold; dropping a raised unit's earlier events, keeping them all, or giving it the later rate of units in its present class each misstates the expected rate.
lineage.stump: The default path drops every claim a building filed before it was elevated and puts the two riverine counties elevated after 2016 in the pilot, because it never asks whether the 2016 water would still have reached the raised floors.

lineage.driver: A total for a period not yet counted is carried from the last complete count by the movement of a fixed sample, and the sample covers a shrinking share of the whole because new members join only the whole, at a pace that differs by area and has held steady through every counted period; carrying the last count by the sample's movement, or scaling the sample by the last count's ratio to it, drops one more period of that drift, so the ratio must be carried forward on its own path.
